Silverscript v1 shipped on Kaspa this week, and the chart noticed.

$KAS tapped the 50-week SMA on a wick.

Three things landed at once and most people only saw one of them...
tweets.hook: Silverscript v1 shipped on Kaspa this week, and the chart noticed.

tweets.text:
One: the tech.

Silverscript compiles straight to Kaspa Script on the L1. No separate VM, no sidechain, no bridge.

Contracts that took thousands of lines of raw opcodes are now about 60 readable lines.

It closes an eight-month build alongside the Toccata hard fork (mainnet June 30).

UTXO programmability: local state per UTXO, covenants, vaults, native assets, on proof of work.

A toolbox instead of an opcode manual.

Two: the chart.

$KAS +17% on the week, +35% on the month, market cap right around $1 billion.

The weekly candle tapped the 50-week SMA on a wick. No close above it yet. The close is a matter of when.

Three: the attention.

Bigger names in this industry started saying Kaspa out loud, more often than ever.

The people who turned their backs realize it is not fading away. The people who never heard of it go look it up.

The macro in the way: PPI 5.4% year over year, the ECB hiked to a year-and-a-half high, Sept 16 Fed hike odds near 60%, $BTC under $80K.

My read: dip through the weekend, sideways a few weeks, then the four-year cycle zombies pile in and turn October green.

If you would rather hear about the Silverscript than the price,

Follow me for Kaspa and macro takes that ignore the four-year cycle echo chamber.

🧠 + 💪

yt_posts.topic: Silverscript v1 shipped on Kaspa the same week $KAS tapped the 50-week SMA
yt_posts.body_style: news breakdown: three Kaspa beats (tech, chart, attention), then the macro timing read
yt_posts.body:
Silverscript v1 shipped on Kaspa this week, and the chart noticed.

Three things landed at once, and if you only watch the price you saw one of them.

First, the tech. Silverscript is a high-level smart contract language that compiles straight down to Kaspa Script on the L1. No separate virtual machine, no sidechain, no bridge. Contracts that used to take thousands of lines of raw opcodes are now about 60 readable lines. It closes an eight-month build alongside the Toccata hard fork that went live on mainnet June 30. This is UTXO programmability: local state per UTXO, covenants, vaults, native asset management, all on a proof of work chain. The team called it a toolbox, and that is the right word. Developers who want to build on Kaspa now have an on-ramp that does not start with an opcode manual, and this is only the beginning; layers of abstraction get added on top of it from here.

Second, the chart. $KAS is up about 17% on the week and 35% on the month, the market cap is sitting right around a billion dollars, and this week the weekly candle tapped the 50-week SMA on a wick. Not a close above it yet. But tapping it at all after this bear market is the tell, and the weekly close above it is a matter of when.

Third, the attention. Bigger names in this industry started saying Kaspa out loud over the last couple of weeks, and it is happening more often than it ever has. That does two things: the people who turned their backs on Kaspa realize it is not fading away, and a whole crowd that never heard of it goes and looks it up.

Now the macro, because it matters for timing. PPI printed 5.4% year over year, the ECB just hiked to its highest rate in a year and a half, and the odds of a Fed hike on September 16 are around 60%. Bitcoin is under $80K. My read: we dip through the weekend pricing in the hike, chop sideways for a few weeks, and then the four-year cycle zombies pile back in and turn October green. The Kaspa dip inside that window is the one I want. Spot, not leverage.

Never financial advice. Never.

So commit to it in the comments: does $KAS close a weekly candle above the 50-week SMA before the Fed decides on the 16th, later this month, or not until October?

Hit like and subscribe if you would rather hear about the Silverscript than the price.

yt_posts.topic: Robinhood added asset pages for JUGGERNAUT and FRONG and both ripped without spot trading
yt_posts.body_style: narrative arc: what Robinhood did, why a page matters, the frog race, the Juggernaut exception
yt_posts.body:
Robinhood put JUGGERNAUT and FRONG on the app this week, and you cannot even buy them there yet.

Read that again. Robinhood added searchable asset pages for two Robinhood Chain memes: you can look them up and watch the price, that is it. No spot trading. JUGGERNAUT ran over 500% in an hour and settled around +380% with volume up 3,000%. FRONG climbed 130% and settled around double, volume up 1,300%. On a search page.

Here is why that is a bigger deal than the numbers. CASHCAT is still the only Robinhood Chain meme you can actually buy on Robinhood, and it ran to a $150 million cap in July off exactly this kind of attention. An asset page is the step before a listing. The chain's DEX did $4.5 billion of volume in 30 days on a network that was built for tokenized stocks. Vlad Tenev said it himself: built for RWA, works great for memes too.

Now the frog. I will be honest: FRONG was never on my candidate list for the official Robinhood frog. Robin the Frog looks like a Muppet to me, and I was rooting for a different frog entirely. But FRONG has the receipts: its frog was the teaser mascot for Uniswap's Pools.trade launchpad, the token was minted six days before the launchpad went public, and a Uniswap product designer launched it himself. First to Pools, a real origin story, decent pumps ever since. That is why it got the page, and Robin the Frog at a $25 million cap is still chasing it.

JUGGERNAUT is simpler, and I was skeptical of it out loud. Historically, a meme built on an existing character never works in crypto; the ones that work are invented for crypto, or were a meme before they were a coin. JUGGERNAUT is the exception for one reason: the photo of Vlad Tenev getting hugged by the Juggernaut on Wall Street is the CEO's favorite meme. That was the entire thesis, and it was enough.

Never financial advice. Never.

So tell me straight in the comments: which one gets actual spot trading on Robinhood first, JUGGERNAUT or FRONG? And if you think neither, and the search page was the top, say that too.
